name: Bar U Ranch: historic ranch, Percheron wagon ride & roping
location: Bar U Ranch National Historic Site, near Longview
ages: All ages; free admission for youth
season: Seasonal; currently closed for the season (as of Oct 13, 2026)
description: Explore 35 historic ranch buildings, meet the Percheron horses on the free wagon shuttle, and try roping a replica steer.

name: Parks Canada Xplorers at Bar U Ranch
location: Bar U Ranch National Historic Site
season: When the site is open; 2026 program renewal may limit availability
description: Kids complete Xplorers challenges while visiting and earn a collectible Parks Canada reward.

name: Bar U Ranch walking trails (Pekisko Creek, Viewpoint, Riparian)
location: Bar U Ranch National Historic Site
season: When the site is open
description: A 3 km creekside trail plus shorter strolls to red chairs and a ridge viewpoint, with shady picnic spots.

name: Ann & Sandy Cross Conservation Area trails
location: Off Hwy 22X, southwest of Calgary (Foothills County)
season: Year-round hiking and snowshoeing; register before visiting
description: About 20 km of interpretive trails through aspen forest and grassland on a protected wildlife area.

name: Cross Conservation Area guided nature programs
location: Off Hwy 22X, Foothills County
season: Year-round, by booking; community events through the year
description: Guided hikes and outdoor conservation education about local plants, wildlife and habitat.

name: Kananaskis public interpretive programs
location: Peter Lougheed PP, Bow Valley PP, McLean Creek PRA and more
season: Mainly summer
description: Free, no-reservation family programs, amphitheatre shows and chats with park interpreters.

name: Animal Hour at William Watson Lodge
location: William Watson Lodge, Peter Lougheed Provincial Park
season: Confirmed dates: Sat Nov 7 and Dec 5, 2026; Jan 16, Feb 13 and Mar 13, 2027, at 1:00 pm (lodge closed Oct 13-17 and Nov 20-25, 2026)
description: Free interactive wildlife talk where kids can ask questions and touch animal artifacts.

name: Peter Lougheed Provincial Park
location: North end of Hwy 40 South, Kananaskis
season: Year-round (reach from the north in winter); check advisories, including bear activity
description: Family trails in summer and snowshoeing in winter in the heart of Kananaskis.

name: Kananaskis Country trails & day-use areas
location: West of Longview / Hwy 22
season: Year-round; some roads gated in winter; Conservation Pass required to park
description: Mountain trails and picnic areas a short drive west of the Foothills towns.

name: Highwood Pass / Hwy 40 South scenic drive
location: Peter Lougheed PP to Highwood House Junction
season: Closed to vehicles Dec 1 - June 14
description: A high-alpine scenic drive with trailheads; go before the Dec 1 closure and dress for mountain weather.

name: Sheep River Provincial Park & Sheep Falls day use
location: West of Turner Valley on Hwy 546
season: Sheep Falls day use open until Nov 30 (season May 15 - Nov 30); Hwy 546 closed west of Sandy McNabb Dec 1 - May 14
description: Waterfall views, picnic tables and fire pits, and wildlife viewing in the Sheep River valley.
advisory: Active Alberta Parks safety advisory: washed-out bridge material in the Sheep River about 100 m downstream of Indian Oils Day Use creates a strainer hazard. Use caution near the water.

name: West Bragg Creek trails
location: West Bragg Creek Provincial Recreation Area
ages: Includes very short loops (e.g., 0.3 km Bunny Loop)
season: Year-round; many trails are winter-only or summer-only; check trail status
description: A big trail network for hiking, snowshoeing and cross-country skiing, with some equestrian trails.

name: Okotoks Erratic (Big Rock)
location: About 10 km west of Okotoks on Hwy 7
season: Year-round
description: A giant glacier-carried boulder with a great story; stay off the rock, a protected Indigenous cultural site.

name: Highwood River fishing
location: Kananaskis Country through High River to the Bow
season: Mostly June 16 - Oct 31; varies by stretch
description: A classic Foothills river with a bait ban and mostly catch-and-release trout; see our fishing page.

name: Family fishing on the Sheep River
location: Sheep River through Diamond Valley (Turner Valley / Black Diamond)
season: Check Alberta regulations
description: The town recommends the Sheep River for family fishing, with Highwood River, Cataract Creek and Chain Lakes nearby.

name: Kids Can Catch (family fishing events)
location: Events across Alberta
season: Event dates posted on the ACA site
description: Free events where mentors help new anglers bait, cast and safely release fish.

name: Family Day Ice Fishing at Chain Lakes
organizer: Okotoks & District Fish and Game Association
location: Chain Lakes Provincial Park (Hwy 22 & Hwy 533, west of Nanton)
season: Held Feb 14, 2026 (Family Fishing Weekend); watch for the 2027 date
description: Free Kids Can Catch ice-fishing day with loaner rods, pre-drilled holes and mentors; RSVP required.

name: Ice fishing safety
location: Province-wide
season: Only once ice is safe
description: Never walk on less than 10 cm of ice and avoid aerated lakes and moving water.

name: Foothills Archery Club
location: Past shoots at Millarville Racetrack and Turner Valley
ages: All ages; past intro program for ages 10+
season: Website last updated 2019; confirm the club is active
description: A volunteer club affiliated with Archery Alberta that welcomes families of all ages and abilities.

name: High River Happy Trails
location: Throughout High River, along the river
season: Year-round
description: Over 19 km of paved pathways along the river and through parks for walking and biking.

name: George Lane Memorial Park
location: Next to downtown High River
season: Year-round; winter outdoor rink and Christmas lights
description: A treed park with a playground and picnic areas, plus skating under the lights and a holiday light display in winter.

name: High River outdoor skating rink
location: 820 Highwood Trail SW, High River
season: Winter, weather-dependent (Chinooks can affect ice)
description: A town-maintained outdoor rink that becomes a ball hockey and basketball court in warmer months.

name: Okotoks pathways, parks & toboggan hills
location: Okotoks, including the Sheep River valley
season: Year-round; 14 outdoor rinks and 6 toboggan hills in winter
description: 100 km of connected pathways, 72 playgrounds, a pump track and BMX track, and winter sledding and skating.

name: Library in the Wild
location: Okotoks Public Library
season: Summer Wednesdays, 1-2 pm (2026 run ended Aug 19); registration required
description: Free outdoor games, crafts and hands-on activities for young kids.

name: Nature Fridays
location: Environmental Education Centre, Okotoks
season: Fridays (e.g., May 22, 2026, 10 am - 4 pm); centre open weekdays
description: Drop-in nature crafts, nature walks and outdoor scavenger hunts led by town staff.

name: Friendship Trail
location: Between Black Diamond and Turner Valley, north of Hwy 22
season: Year-round
description: A gentle 3 km paved trail with viewpoints, rock formations and the old coal mine site.

name: Diamond Valley Bike Pump Track
location: Erma Joy Brown Park, Black Diamond
season: Dawn to dusk; free
description: A looping dirt track with bumps and berms for pedal bikes.

name: Skating on natural ice (safety)
location: Province-wide
season: Winter
description: Ice should be 15 cm to skate alone and 20 cm for games; avoid ponds over running water.
